solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Starchy cereal principally served in the past

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, at the head, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

blocks.note: first letter of served
ago means in the past, as in 'years ago'

explanation.surface: A dinner lady recalls the starchy cereal mostly dished up in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch extracted from palm pith, used as a grain-like food in puddings.

clue.text: Small number crossing river, the UK's longest

indicators.note: a number crossing something lies across it, so it is split around the other piece

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an even number, such as two or four
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A modest number of people cross the UK's longest river.
explanation.walkthrough: S is placed first, then EVEN wraps around R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn, flowing from Wales through England to the Bristol Channel, is the longest river in Britain.

clue.text: Club accommodating old vessel

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one word holds the other within it

blocks.note: a bat is the club used in cricket or baseball
O is a common abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A sailing club finds room for an elderly vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Vessel in the nautical sense is any craft that travels on water, which is what a boat is.

clue.text: Resolve to put off race crossing major road

indicators.note: a race crossing a road straddles it, so the road ends up inside the other words

blocks.note: to deter is to discourage or put off
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords
a race or people, a nation

explanation.surface: A firm decision to postpone a race that would cross a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: The race and the putting off together straddle the road. The M1 is Britain's main motorway, from London to Leeds, written MI in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a noun means firmness of purpose, a synonym for determination.

clue.text: Leader of union forcing rebellion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever comes at its front, its initial letter

blocks.note: first letter of union
prising means forcing open, as with a lever

explanation.surface: A trade union boss provokes a revolt among the members.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority, the same thing as a rebellion.

clue.text: Dry land reduced to powder

blocks.note: first meaning: the solid surface of the earth, as opposed to sea
second meaning: past participle of grind, as with coffee

explanation.surface: Parched earth crumbles into dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the earth underfoot, and the past participle of grind describes something milled to fine particles.

clue.text: Purchase cheap newspaper during formal reception

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits within its span, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper
a levee is a formal reception, originally one held by a monarch on rising

explanation.surface: Someone buys a tabloid in the middle of a formal reception.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase looks like buying, but here it is the noun meaning grip or mechanical advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or mechanical advantage, which is exactly what leverage provides.

clue.text: Woodland plant, one with unusual name

indicators.note: unusual suggests the words are not in their normal form, so their letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a woodland plant that has an odd name.
explanation.definitionFit: The wood anemone is a white-flowered spring plant common on woodland floors.

clue.text: Onset of primitive impulse to eradicate

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of primitive
an urge is an impulse or desire

explanation.surface: The first stirrings of a primal instinct to wipe something out.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid something of unwanted elements, a synonym for eradicate.

clue.text: Plain retired vicar dipping into Holy Writ

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, gone back, so the abbreviation is read backwards
dipping into something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend, a vicar's title
OT is the Old Testament, part of Holy Writ

explanation.surface: A retired clergyman leafs through the Bible in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and unconcealed, so plain in the sense of obvious.

clue.text: Gourmet cooked pie to preserve

indicators.note: something cooked is changed from its raw state, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A food lover bakes a pie meant to be kept.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and drink, a synonym for gourmet.

clue.text: Study horse's previous record — and go with the stream

blocks.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn by heart
form is a racehorse's record of past performances

explanation.surface: A punter checks a horse's past results and then backs the favourite like everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Con meaning study is a crossword staple from older English.
explanation.definitionFit: Going with the stream means following the crowd, which is what someone who conforms does.

clue.text: Stop, for example, in Hebridean island

blocks.note: a colon is a punctuation stop
say introduces an example, as in 'a fruit, say, an apple'

explanation.surface: A traveller breaks a journey on a Scottish island, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are the islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Colonsay is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Strange chaps originally transmitting such miscellaneous items

indicators.note: originally points to the origin or start of each following word, so their initials are used

blocks.note: odd means strange
chaps are men
first letters of transmitting and such

explanation.surface: Peculiar men start broadcasting an assortment of bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover odds and ends, a mixed collection of bits of various kinds.

clue.text: Support part of UK backing Asian republic

indicators.note: backing means moving in the rear direction, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: aid means support or help
NI is Northern Ireland, one of the UK's four nations

explanation.surface: Part of Britain lends its backing to a republic in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like more support, but it turns the whole of the wordplay around, not just one word.
explanation.definitionFit: India became a republic in 1950 and is the largest country of South Asia.

clue.text: Clear-headed law lord covering island group

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the outer word encloses the other

blocks.note: Lud, as in 'm'lud', is how a judge is addressed in British courts
CI is the Channel Islands, off the coast of Normandy

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted senior judge oversees a group of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid describes someone thinking sanely and rationally, the same as clear-headed.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink a girl takes to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means at the very start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: Clare is a girl's name
first letter of takes

explanation.surface: A young woman starts having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Some retired people wear one near formal strip

blocks.note: nigh is an old word for near
a tie is a strip of cloth worn with formal dress

explanation.surface: Pensioners put on something close to formal dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests pensioners, but it means gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is the garment many people put on when they have gone to bed for the night.

clue.text: Story about king, one in early film

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word goes round the inserted letters

blocks.note: a tale is a story
K is the chess abbreviation for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tale about a monarch features in an old movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkies were the first films with synchronised sound, replacing silent movies in the late 1920s.

clue.text: Take courses in shelter? That's most clever

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the eating goes within the shelter

blocks.note: eating a meal means taking its courses
a nest is a shelter for birds

explanation.surface: Is dining under cover the smartest idea?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' suggests study, but here they are the parts of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can mean clever or ingenious, as in a neat trick, so the superlative is most clever.

clue.text: Sanctimonious bunch making TV try-out

blocks.note: pi is short for pious, meaning sanctimonious
a lot is a group or bunch

explanation.surface: A self-righteous group of people produces a trial episode for television.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial episode made to test whether a television series will be commissioned.

clue.text: When speaking, beg for quarry

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is judged by how it sounds out loud, not its spelling

blocks.note: to pray can mean to beg or plead, as in 'pray, tell me'

explanation.surface: A hunter pleads out loud for their quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarry means the animal being hunted, the same thing as prey.

clue.text: Going north, obtained a historical garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

blocks.note: got means obtained
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heading north, someone acquires a piece of period dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the draped outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Go-between — a pukka fellow!

blocks.note: taken as written
a gent is a gentleman, a proper or pukka fellow

explanation.surface: A middleman is hailed as a thoroughly decent chap.
explanation.walkthrough: Pukka is Anglo-Indian slang meaning genuine or proper.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on behalf of others, negotiating between two parties as an intermediary.

clue.text: Oscar, writing half-heartedly, finds opportunity

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly loses half its heart, so one of the two central letters is dropped

blocks.note: Oscar is the NATO alphabet word for O
penning means writing

explanation.surface: Oscar, writing without enthusiasm, still gets a big chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of PENNING is its double N; losing one of them leaves PENING.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a chance or vacancy, as in a job opening, so a synonym for opportunity.
